title: Effect of calcium carbonate on the absorption of levothyroxine
authors: Singh N, Singh PN, Hershman JM
followUp: 3 months of calcium carbonate with levothyroxine, then 2 months after stopping calcium
population: Patients with hypothyroidism on stable levothyroxine (Synthroid) at a Veterans Affairs endocrine clinic; before-during-after design without a control group, plus in vitro binding experiments
funder: Funding statement not read: the publisher page displayed no funding or acknowledgment section, although PubMed indexes the article as research supported by non-US-government sources.
result: 1200 mg/d of elemental calcium as calcium carbonate was taken together with levothyroxine for 3 months. Mean free T4 was 17 pmol/l before, 15 during and 18 after calcium; mean TSH 1.6, 2.7 and 1.4 mIU/l (P = .008). TSH rose in 13 of 20 patients during calcium and exceeded the normal range in 4 (20%), highest 7.8 mIU/l. In vitro, T4 adsorbed to calcium carbonate at acidic pH (52% of T4 left in supernatant at 400 mg/ml at pH 2.0) but not at pH 7.4.
